applicabilityConditions.absenceDefinition: a species was treated as lacking a DFA if it had no DFA hit and also had more than 6,000 proteins in UniProt the criteria are liberal and likely produce false negatives, especially for species with far more than 6,000 proteins, so DFA prevalence across the fungal tree is probably underestimated
applicabilityConditions.note: conclusions are bounded by which traits had usable public data, not by which traits are biologically plausible
applicabilityConditions.phylogeny: TimeTree database web interface; the resulting tree represented 85 fungal orders
applicabilityConditions.proteinFamily: structurally divergent fungal actins, defined as ProteinCartography clusters LC04, LC11 and LC14
applicabilityConditions.statistics: model selection comparing a model in which DFA presence/absence and the trait share an evolutionary trajectory against a model in which they evolved independently, scored by Akaike information criterion where the lowest AIC wins phylogeny-corrected generalized linear mixed model (logistic regression) testing whether variation in the continuous trait accounts for variation in DFA status while controlling for shared evolutionary history; a slope significantly different from zero would indicate a correlation
applicabilityConditions.traitSource: Fun Fun: aggregates species-level ecological, cellular and biochemical trait information from multiple studies, including FUNGuild classifications of ecological function and trophic mode
applicabilityConditions.unitOfObservation: species, not independent observations; phylogenetic non-independence is modelled explicitly

confidence.basis: lability is inferred partly from inferred absences, and the authors note that overestimating absence would overestimate lability

cost.note: computational study; 853 species in the working set, 102 analysed; no monetary or compute cost is reported

stages.label: ProteinCartography structure search and clustering
stages.method: search mode with standard parameters; 3,000 Foldseek hits requested per input protein, 6,000 total proteins per input; Leiden clustering on the all-versus-all structural similarity matrix; similarity by TM-score from TM-align, where above 0.5 suggests structural similarity and below 0.17 indicates unrelated proteins

parameters.compactnessThreshold: clusters with compactness above 0.6 treated as well defined

stages.label: working-set definition and trait curation
stages.method: a species was treated as lacking a DFA if it had no DFA hit and also had more than 6,000 proteins in UniProt. chosen to maximise overlap between species with trait information and species with known DFA status, and to include biological features for which actin is relevant. 13 species whose DFA status varied across strains were removed after BLASTp and tBLASTn checks proved uninterpretable, possibly from undersampling or noisy assemblies. 28 further species removed for absence from TimeTree.
stages.note: category levels were redefined after seeing the data, to keep at least four species per level

parameters.thresholdSensitivityCheck: varying the threshold from 6,000 to 25,000 proteins did not greatly change the ratio of species with to without a DFA (40:60 at 10,000; 44:56 at 20,000; 42:58 at 25,000)

protocolAdaptations: varying the threshold from 6,000 to 25,000 proteins did not greatly change the ratio of species with to without a DFA (40:60 at 10,000; 44:56 at 20,000; 42:58 at 25,000)
categorical trait levels were redefined to maximise the number of categories containing four or more species, because categories with fewer than four species would not support the model
growth form: yeast and facultative yeast collapsed into yeast; ergot, cordyceptoid, rust and xylaroid removed
trophic mode: three levels saprotroph, pathotroph, symbiotroph; species with multiple modes counted into each
ascus dehiscence: fissitunicate and rostrate removed
auxin-responsive promoter: promoter count transformed into a binary present/absent variable
